I farm the way that protects my harvest first and keeps the work manageable for my family. Since my land is only 10.9 mu and some people in my household work off-farm, I will keep the main part of the farm in my usual wheat-maize rotation because that is the most familiar and dependable arrangement for me. I have well irrigation, so I will use that to stabilize wheat and maize when rainfall is not enough. I will put 8 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 8 mu, and I will keep 2.9 mu in cotton because cotton still gives me a cash crop and spreads my risk. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and stand establishment, but I will not push inputs too hard because I want a balance between cost and output. For wheat, I will use moderate fertilizer, a few irrigations, and a small number of pesticide sprays because I mainly want a steady grain yield. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, enough nitrogen to support strong summer growth, and fewer irrigations because summer rain helps. For cotton, I will manage it more carefully for pests and keep fertilizer moderate, because cotton needs more attention through the season. I will use rotary tillage on most fields because it is practical for me and fits my usual way of preparing land.
